audit.whatIsWrong: Graves's passive, New Destiny, is not mentioned anywhere in either layer — specifically that his four bullets cannot pass through units, and that he must reload after spending his ammo.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Attacks fire 4 bullets, which cannot pass through units" and "He must reload when he runs out of ammo." For a melee tank walking at a ranged carry, minion body-blocking is the single most effective counterplay in the matchup, and the reload gap is the concrete window in which to close distance. Both were absent, and the entry instead built its whole approach around a cooldown that Graves can refund.
audit.corrected: Added minion body-blocking and the reload window as the primary early-lane plan.

audit.whatIsWrong: Quickdraw is named the matchup-defining cooldown in eight strings — tldr (twice), breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.early, breakdown.mid, phases[1].why, phases[3].why, phases[5].why and dosFull[0] — with instructions to engage "when it is down".
audit.why: Quickdraw is 16/15/14/13/12s but Riot's text adds that "hitting enemies with basic attacks lowers the cooldown of this skill". A Graves who is auto-attacking the wave is continuously refunding it, so it is rarely down at any predictable moment. Worse, dashing toward a champion grants him two stacks of True Grit, so the ability he is supposedly punished for using also makes him tankier. The reliable window is the reload gap, not a cooldown.
audit.corrected: Re-pointed the tracked window to the reload gap and noted that autos refund Quickdraw.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text says "his Smoke Screen (W) blinds your follow-up". Smoke Screen does not blind.
audit.why: Riot's text: it creates "a cloud of smoke that reduces sight range", with magic damage and a brief slow on the initial impact. That is a nearsight effect, not a blind — Zac's abilities and attacks still land at full effect, he simply cannot see out of the cloud. The distinction matters because a player who believes they are blinded will abort a committed engage that would actually have worked.
audit.corrected: Restated it as a sight-range cut rather than a blind.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing mentions that End of the Line detonates on terrain contact.
audit.why: Riot's text: the shell "detonates after 1 second, or after colliding with terrain". Against a wall the detonation happens immediately instead of after the travel delay, so a Zac who hugs terrain to avoid being flanked is standing exactly where the Q pays off best. This is concrete, actionable positioning that was stated nowhere.
audit.corrected: Added the terrain detonation to whys[0].
sources: champ-data/_kits/graves.json (End of the Line, terrain flag)

audit.whatIsWrong: The layers disagree at levels 2 and 3: content reads Graves/Graves/Graves/Zac/Graves/Zac/Zac, full reads Graves/Skill/Zac/Zac/Graves/Zac/Zac.
audit.why: The content chart is right and its own prose supports it — spikes[0] identifies level 4 as Zac's spike and whys[2] says Graves still poke-bursts him at 3. The full layer awarding Zac level 3 contradicts that. The rest of the chart is well-calibrated for a 50.81% matchup over 433 games, which is the largest sample in the slice.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2] pairs "Pick up every blob" with a body about Graves wasting Quickdraw, and dontsFull[1] pairs "Let him stomp blobs" with "Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown".
audit.why: The same generator template mismatch present in all nine Zac entries I audited.
audit.corrected: Re-pointed both bodies at their titles.

notes: Largest sample in the slice (433 games, 50.81%) and the chart was already well-calibrated — only levels 2 and 3 disagreed across layers. The substantive gap was point 4: Graves's passive is never mentioned in either layer, and it contains the two most useful facts in the matchup for a melee tank. His four bullets cannot pass through units, so minion body-blocking simply switches his damage off, and he must reload after emptying his ammo, which is the concrete window to walk him down. Instead the entry pointed at Quickdraw in eight separate strings as the cooldown to punish — but Graves refunds Quickdraw by auto-attacking, and dashing toward a champion grants him two True Grit stacks, so the ability he is 'punished' for using also makes him tankier. That is the fourth entry in this slice built on a cooldown that does not behave like a fixed window (Gangplank's Powder Keg, Gnar's GNAR!, Gragas's Body Slam were the others); the generator appears to pick one enemy ability per matchup and assume it is a static, waitable cooldown. Also corrected: Smoke Screen was described as blinding. It reduces sight range — Zac's abilities land normally, he just cannot see out — and a player who thinks they are blinded will abort an engage that would have worked.
